propositions: When push recovery's dirty-merge encounters an untracked local file that collides with a file the remote merge wants to create, the merge aborts with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' and today's code fails to recover
The same compaction-leftover untracked-overwrite collision class already wedges reconverge, but reconverge has self-healing logic that push recovery lacks
Push recovery must quarantine named colliding untracked paths into a shared directory and retry the merge once to match reconverge's recovery pattern
The stash commit object holding tracked edits must be restored exactly once on every exit path (success, retry-failure, non-recoverable abort)
Push recovery must reuse the shared parser from sync without duplicating recovery logic, while using late-bound core._git to preserve existing monkeypatch boundaries
